eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign near-certainty to a 26°C maximum in Mexico City on September 4 because official station observations and quality-controlled data releases confirm that peak reading. Early September climatology places typical daytime highs between 22–26°C under the influence of the North American monsoon’s waning phase, with afternoon convection and moderate humidity limiting further warming. Model guidance issued 24–48 hours prior aligned closely with this outcome, showing limited spread across ensembles. Revisions to the official record, discrepancies between primary urban stations and surrounding sites, or post-processing adjustments for instrument calibration remain the only realistic paths that could alter resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus favoring a 90-91°F peak in Miami on September 5 reflects National Weather Service and model guidance for a mostly sunny morning with highs near or slightly above 89°F before afternoon thunderstorms develop. High humidity and southeasterly flow support surface temperatures climbing into the lower 90s early in the day, consistent with early September climatology where Miami averages around 89-90°F. The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klax

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus from meteorological agencies and models centers on a daytime high of 28–29°C in the Incheon/Seoul area on September 6 under mostly clear skies and moderate northeast winds.** Persistent high pressure and dry northeasterly flow have suppressed cloud development and moisture, keeping conditions stable after earlier September warmth. Official guidance, including hourly profiles showing peaks near 28°C with limited diurnal spread, supports this range, while minor model differences in boundary-layer mixing or exact wind timing account for the small probabilities assigned to 30°C or 27°C. Traders have priced the 54% implied probability on 29°C to reflect the tight clustering of guidance around the upper end of that interval, with resolution depending on the official Incheon station maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models for September 6, 2026, in Amsterdam converge on a daily maximum near 22°C, aligning with the market's strongest implied probability at 52.5%.** 

Multiple sources, including WeatherBug (73°F / ~23°C), Globalmeteo (~22°C), and Meteocanada (23°C), project highs in the 21–23°C range under partly cloudy skies and light southerly flow. This represents a modest increase over the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 20.2°C for the date. Recent conditions show cooler readings around 19–20°C on September 5, with the shift tied to evolving pressure patterns favoring mild advection rather than strong warming or cooling. 

Lower probabilities for 20°C or below (under 5% combined) reflect limited downside risk from current model runs, while 24°C+ remains a low-probability outlier (around 4%) absent unexpected clear-sky intensification. Resolution depends on official observations, likely from Schiphol or KNMI stations, with final model updates expected overnight into the morning of the 6th. Traders appear to be weighting the tight clustering of ensemble guidance around the 22°C threshold.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Dallas Love Field Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kdal

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent high-pressure ridging across the southern Plains is driving the current market-implied odds favoring a Dallas high of 98–101 °F on September 6. National Weather Service and model consensus indicate mostly sunny conditions with southerly flow advecting warm, moist air, supporting daytime maxima near 99–101 °F and heat indices exceeding 105 °F. This setup follows several days of similar readings above the 1991–2020 climatological average of 92.5 °F. With the ridge expected to hold through the weekend and minimal cloud cover or precipitation in short-range guidance, traders have priced in limited downside risk to the 96–97 °F bin or upside into the low 100s absent any unexpected model shift before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: A cold front advancing across southern Brazil combined with a polar air mass has sharply lowered expected highs in São Paulo for September 6, positioning 15–17 °C as the market’s leading outcomes. Official guidance and ensemble models from sources including the National Meteorological Institute and European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts indicate an overcast day with widespread light rain, southeasterly winds of 20–30 km/h, and daytime maxima most likely between 13 °C and 16 °C after early-morning readings near 16 °C. This represents a 6–10 °C drop from early-September norms. Traders are assigning the highest implied probability to 16 °C, reflecting the tight clustering of recent model runs around that value while still allowing modest upside to 17 °C or downside to 15 °C depending on exact timing of the front’s passage. Updated high-resolution forecasts and surface observations issued in the next 24–48 hours will further refine resolution criteria.
